races.title: State House, District 110
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Caroline Eason
cands.bio: Pharmacist and third-generation independent community pharmacist who works at her family's pharmacy chain. Republican from Lawndale. She defeated eight-term incumbent Kelly Hastings in the March 2026 primary and won the November 2026 general election for NC House District 110. She has held no prior elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace or when she may have moved to North Carolina. We found no record of actions in office, since she has not held one, and no bills she has sponsored. We found no statements from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her site mentions only 'managed growth' and 'strengthen public education', without specifics. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and no endorsements or controversies turned up in the pages reviewed. Her work history and background come mostly from her campaign site and Wikipedia.

local.label: Roots 90: She grew up in Lawndale and is described as an upper-Cleveland County native who graduated from Burns High School, but her birthplace is not stated in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Doctor of Pharmacy from UNC Chapel Hill; works at her family's independent pharmacy chain; had a health policy role in her final doctoral year; testified before the NC House Health Committee on a bill; no prior elected office.
qual.why: Her real-world work is in a family small-business pharmacy, which fits the middle band for business roles. She has no legislative service and a short work record, so she sits at the low end of that band. Her advisory committee seat and testimony add nothing to the score.

cands.name: Mary Silver
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 110 in 2026. She advanced without a primary and lost the general election to Republican Caroline Eason. No other biographical or career details were found.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended by two voter-guide groups, Better Future NC (Cam Pruette) and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (Tevin Davis). Both are described there as Sway voting groups.

cands.gaps: We found no information on where Mary Silver was born or raised, when she came to North Carolina, or her work history, so her ties to the state and her job fit for the office could not be assessed. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. We found no stated positions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing, and no records of actions she has taken on these. We found no news coverage, controversies or foreign ties.
